Mapping out of pasted squares

The pushout pasting proof applies the pullback pasting lemma after mapping out. This requires comparing the specified matching identifications on the two routes. The calculation uses the Chapter 1 mapping-anima and pullback structure; functor categories are not needed.

Consider adjacent squares \(L,R\) with top arrows \(g_1\colon A_1\to A_2\), \(g_2\colon A_2\to A_3\), bottom arrows \(h_1\colon B_1\to B_2\), \(h_2\colon B_2\to B_3\), vertical arrows \(f_i\colon A_i\to B_i\), and matchings \[ \lambda \colon f_2g_1=h_1f_1,\qquad \rho \colon f_3g_2=h_2f_2. \] Their pasted square \(O\) uses the matching from \(f_3(g_2g_1)\) to \((h_2h_1)f_1\) obtained by reassociating, applying \(\rho \) along \(g_1\), reassociating, applying \(h_2\) to \(\lambda \), and reassociating back. The matching is part of the input, as well as the four boundary functors.

Supplementary Lemma 1. For an absolute category \(X\), put \(L_X(f)=\mathrm {id}_X\times f\), and write \(\kappa _X(f,g)\colon L_X(g)L_X(f)=L_X(gf)\) for its chosen composition comparison. The product images of \(L,R\) paste to a cocone which compares with the product image of \(O\), after changing the upper span arrow by \(\kappa _X(g_1,g_2)\). The comparison has the identity on the left leg and \(\kappa _X(h_1,h_2)\) on the right leg, with compatibility of the matchings.

Proof idea

Expand the pasted matching into its five stages. Compatibility with inverse associators handles the first and last stages. Naturality of the product composition comparison handles the two whiskered matchings, and its associativity comparison handles the middle stage. Paste these five comparison squares and cancel the common outer composition comparison. Postcomposition by any functor \(X\times B_3\to E\) preserves the resulting whole-cocone comparison. □

For \(k\colon A\to B\), write \(k^*\colon \Map (B,E)\to \Map (A,E)\) for precomposition by \(k\).

Supplementary Lemma 2. For an absolute category \(E\), let \(M_E(L)\), \(M_E(R)\), and \(M_E(O)\) be the mapping-out cones. Pasting \(M_E(R)\) and \(M_E(L)\), in this reversed order, and changing its left cospan arrow by \[ \kappa _g\colon g_1^*g_2^*=(g_2g_1)^* \] produces a cone with a specified comparison to \(M_E(O)\). This comparison includes its matching equation, without any pushout hypothesis on \(L\) or \(R\).

Proof idea

Use the universal parameter \(X=\Map (B_3,E)\) and uncurry the mapping-out cones at its identity. The composition comparison for precomposition on mapping animae evaluates to the product comparison \(\kappa _X\). The two square matchings evaluate to the corresponding product cocones, postcomposed with evaluation \(X\times B_3\to E\).

Apply Supplementary Lemma 1 and reflect the resulting whole-cocone comparison through uncurrying. This reflection is available because \(X\) is an anima. Finally remove restriction by the identity with the cone unit comparison.

If \(U,V\) denote the source and target cones over a common cospan \((p,q)\), and \(a,b\) the constructed leg comparisons, the retained equation is \[ \operatorname {match}(V)\cdot (p\star a) =(q\star b)\cdot \operatorname {match}(U). \] Here \(\star \) denotes whiskering and vertical composition applies the rightmost factor first. The witnesses \(a,b\) are those constructed by uncurrying and reflection; the assertion includes their compatibility. □

Supplementary Corollary 3. If \(L\) is a pushout, then \(R\) is a pushout if and only if the specified pasted square \(O\) is a pushout.

Proof idea

For every \(E\), the mapping-out cone \(M_E(L)\) is a pullback. Contravariance makes it the fixed right square in the pullback pasting argument. Pasting and cancellation therefore identify the pullback conditions for \(M_E(R)\) and the pasted mapping cone. Changing the cospan arrow by \(\kappa _g\) preserves the pullback property. Supplementary Lemma 2 transfers it to \(M_E(O)\), including the specified matching. Quantify over \(E\). □
